response.sql: WITH side_counts AS (SELECT o.dealedge, COUNT(DISTINCT o.orderspivot) AS order_count FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault WHERE o.dealedge IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.dealedge), side_average AS (SELECT AVG(order_count) AS avg_count FROM side_counts) SELECT SUM(sc.order_count) AS total_count, AVG(sc.order_count - sa.avg_count) AS average_excess FROM side_counts AS sc CROSS JOIN side_average AS sa WHERE sc.order_count > sa.avg_count

assumptions.assumption: Each matched order is counted once per side, even if it has multiple risk/margin records; the average uses sides present among matched orders.

alternatives.interpretation: Count each matched risk/margin record, so an order with multiple risk/margin records contributes multiple times.
alternatives.sql: WITH side_counts AS (SELECT o.dealedge, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM riskandmargin AS r JOIN orders AS o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault WHERE o.dealedge IS NOT NULL GROUP BY o.dealedge), side_average AS (SELECT AVG(match_count) AS avg_count FROM side_counts) SELECT SUM(sc.match_count) AS total_count, AVG(sc.match_count - sa.avg_count) AS average_excess FROM side_counts AS sc CROSS JOIN side_average AS sa WHERE sc.match_count > sa.avg_count
